messages:
alice: Nightly eval spike — v2.7.0-rc3 shows a big drop vs v2.6 on several prompt suites (support, summarization). F1 down ~6% on CUSTOMER_SUPPORT prompts. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/models/rc3/eval/1763456789 :eyes:
nightly-evals-bot: [ALERT] model=v2.7.0-rc3 suite=CUSTOMER_SUPPORT metric=f1 previous=0.78 current=0.73 delta=-0.05 job=eval-1763456789
ben: ugh. any obvious diffs in the model card? tokenizer version bump? quantization flags?
carol: quick check — metadata shows tokenizer_version=2026-03-01, merges=50000 -> was 49992 on v2.6. Also quant_bits=4 (qat) vs previous=8 (fp16) for the candidate. That seems like a big change.
alice: oh — rc3 was a quantization experiment flattened into the weights share. I thought we kept a fp16 fallback. maybe not. sample bad generations in the artifact: 
```
PROMPT: "Customer: My bill shows a charge I didn't make. Help me."
v2.6 OUTPUT: "Sorry to hear that. Can you share the invoice ID and date? I can start a dispute and refund if unauthorized."
v2.7.0-rc3 OUTPUT: "You were charged because you upgraded to Premium. No refunds. Check your settings."
```
ben: that reply is a factual hallucination and tone shift — sounds like tokenization or id-to-embedding mismatch causing context misinterpretation.
dmitri: ran a quick compare: ran `run_local_infer --model rc3 --seed 42 --prompt-file samples/support_20.txt --temp 0.0` and `--model v2.6` differences below (short): rc3 has higher token-embedding L2 diff at input layer ~0.18 average (v2.6 baseline ~0.02).
carol: L2 that big points to tokenizer mismatch or vocabulary reordering. Did the merge table reorder common tokens? We had a script that rebalanced merges because of new training data.
alice: checking tokenizer files in artifact bucket now: s3://redwood-artifacts/models/v2.7.0-rc3/tokenizer/* — vocab_size=50256 but token-to-id mapping changed for indices 1024..1040 (common punctuation + 'refund').
ben: so generation maps prompt tokens to different embeddings -> downstream misunderstood 'refund' as some infrequent token, causing model to latch onto training prior.
dmitri: also noticed compile flags: `--kernel=auto` picked a different fused attention kernel on A100 with seq=1024; combined with quant4 it may amplify representation drift.
carol: possible triage steps: 1) re-run eval with rc3 but swap tokenizer to v2.6 tokenizer (same weights) to isolate tokenizer vs weights. 2) re-run rc3 with 8-bit quant fallback to see quant impact. 3) sanity-check embedding matrix similarity: `cos_sim(E_rc3[:, :10000], E_v2.6[:, :10000])`.
alice: starting step 1 now (weights rc3 + token_map v2.6). posting quick results in a bit. :hourglass:
nightly-evals-bot: queued job eval-1763456920 (swap-tokenizer). status=running
ben: if swap-tokenizer fixes, that's a release-blocker. prefer revert tokenizer changes or pin tokenizer_version to previous for canary.
dmitri: quick run done: swap-tokenizer -> f1 on CUSTOMER_SUPPORT recovers to 0.77 (almost baseline). So tokenizer delta explains most but not all. Quant still accounts for residual -0.01.
carol: good signal. next run: rc3 weights + rc3 tokenizer + quant_bits=8 (force higher precision) to quantify quant impact.
alice: queued: eval-1763457055 (quant-ablation).
dmitri: while we wait, note two operational things: 1) model metadata didn't include `tokenizer_checksum` in the release manifest (we removed it for rc3 accidentally). 2) our canary rollout policy allowed rc3 to reach 5% production before nightly flagged it — need a stricter quality gate when tokenizer or tokenizer_version changes.
ben: agreed. create a quick ticket to block canary if tokenizer_checksum != prev_checksum. assign to release-owner.
carol: results for quant-ablation: forcing 8-bit bring f1 to 0.775 with rc3 tokenizer swapped in. So quant4 causes ~0.005-0.01 degradation beyond tokenizer reordering. Quant amplifies small tokenizer-induced shifts.
alice: plan: 1) stop rc3 canary and revert to v2.6 in prod. 2) build a patch: either restore old tokenizer mapping (preferred) or include tokenizer_version pinned plus checksum check. 3) re-run quant experiments on a stable tokenizer branch. 4) add unit test to eval runner: token->id stability test across minor model bumps.
dmitri: i'll open the rollback PR + incident ticket: INC-1763457100. tagging release-owner @ben.
ben: noted. also propose immediate hotfix to recorder: add manifest validation to CI that `tokenizer_checksum` exists and matches baseline when merging release branches.
alice: adding eval artifacts and minimal repro to the ticket. Pasted minimal repro here: 
```
# reproduce locally
python -m redwood.infer --model /models/v2.7.0-rc3 --tokenizer /tokenizers/v2.6 --prompt "My bill has a charge I didn't make"
# should not produce: "You were charged because you upgraded to Premium. No refunds."
```
carol: also logging this as a regression case for the nightly suite so we can catch token->id map shifts earlier. I'll add a new check in eval harness: compute token id mapping diff and fail if >0.1% of common tokens changed.
dmitri: closing loop: rollback started. canary paused. I'll follow up on quantization ablation branch next week. :lock:
alice: thanks all. takeaway: DO NOT change tokenizer merges/vocab without explicit manifest checksum and gated eval. leaving notes in the release checklist. :memo:
ben: +1 :thumbsup:
nightly-evals-bot: [RESOLVED] job=eval-1763456920 status=complete result=regression_root_cause=tokenizer_mapping
